R.1.synopsis: Approves the construction project plan for the Harrison Community Village, a shelter project presented by the Joint Office of Homeless Services, under the County's FAC-1 procedure. An amendment passed unanimously first; Commissioner Meieran voted no on the plan.

R.2.synopsis: Emergency ordinance amending the County zoning code (Chapter 39) to add a reference to the standards that apply in the Significant Environmental Concern for Streams overlay zone.

R.3.synopsis: Approves the Library Capital Bond Program's St. Johns Library project plan to proceed with construction and authorizes the Chair to sign a guaranteed maximum price amendment.

R.1.synopsis: Approves the County's 2025 state legislative agenda.

R.3.synopsis: Approves an agreement reserving a block of rooms at a motel at 1125 N. Schmeer Road in Portland.

R.4.synopsis: Budget modification authorizing five positions, a lease, security and other operating costs for the County's deflection center.

R.5.synopsis: Budget modification transferring cash for the Coordinated Care Pathway Center project. Commissioner Meieran voted no.

R.3.synopsis: Second reading and adoption of an ordinance amending and reorganizing the Significant Environmental Concern regulations in the County zoning code (Chapter 39).

R.4.synopsis: Approves negotiating the sale of the Gresham Library building at 385 NW Miller Ave. to the City of Gresham, with a leaseback to the County.

R.5.synopsis: Increases the Joint Office of Homeless Services' federal and state funds by $11.4 million and reduces its Supportive Housing Services fund by $4.2 million.

S.1.title: Appointment to fill the vacancy in Oregon Senate District 17 (joint meeting with the Washington County Board of Commissioners).
S.1.synopsis: Meeting jointly with Washington County's commissioners, the Board voted to appoint Lisa Reynolds to fill the vacancy in Oregon Senate District 17; the other nominees were Joel Shapiro and Pradnya Patil. The minutes record the roll call as unanimous.

R.3.synopsis: Second reading and adoption of an ordinance adding Section 29.503(E) to the County's building regulations (Code Chapter 29).

R.2.synopsis: Consents to Chair Vega Pederson's appointment of Annie Lewis as director of Multnomah County Libraries.

R.3.synopsis: Second reading of an ordinance amending the County business income tax (Code Chapter 12) to conform its confidentiality provisions to state law. The minutes record a unanimous roll call.

R.4.synopsis: Second reading of an ordinance amending the Preschool for All income tax (Code Chapter 11.500) to conform its confidentiality provisions to state law and make administrative changes. The minutes record a unanimous roll call.

R.2.synopsis: Approves the Library Capital Bond Program's Belmont Library project plan to proceed with construction and authorizes the Chair to sign a guaranteed maximum price amendment.

R.4.synopsis: Reclassifies seven positions in the Chief Operating Officer's office. Commissioner Brim-Edwards voted no.
Appropriates $3.9 million from the Preschool for All fund contingency to add 174 new mid-year preschool seats. Commissioner Meieran voted no.

R.3.synopsis: Approves the staff recommendation for the bridge type of the east span of the Earthquake Ready Burnside Bridge.

R.1.synopsis: Approves the East County Homelessness Resource Center project plan to proceed with construction under the County's FAC-1 procedure.

R.3.synopsis: Sets County land use fees after a public hearing and repeals Resolution 2023-057. Commissioner Meieran voted no.

R.4.synopsis: Second reading of an ordinance that would have delayed the scheduled increase in the Preschool for All tax and required a technical advisory group report. The motion failed on a 2–2 tie: Commissioners Meieran and Brim-Edwards voted yes, Commissioner Stegmann and Chair Vega Pederson no, and Commissioner Beason was excused.

R.2.synopsis: Adds City of Portland planning code changes to the County's comprehensive plan, zoning map and zoning code (the agenda title is cut off in the minutes).

R.4.synopsis: Resolution urging the Chair to pause the opening of the County's deflection center. After three amendment votes, it failed 2–2: Commissioners Meieran and Brim-Edwards voted yes, Commissioner Beason and Chair Vega Pederson no, and Commissioner Stegmann was excused.

R.3.synopsis: Approves the Library Capital Bond Program's Northwest Library project plan to proceed with construction and authorizes the Chair to sign a guaranteed maximum price amendment.

3003._note: R.4 (AMR ambulance staffing change) was discussed but the minutes record no vote on it.

R.3.synopsis: Adopts accountability and progress measures for the Homelessness Response System, as amended. Only three commissioners voted: the minutes' roll calls on the amendment and the resolution list Brim-Edwards, Stegmann and Vega Pederson, and the Chair thanks 'both' of the others present, so Meieran and Beason are recorded as absent.

R.2.synopsis: Adopts revised rules for the County's Public Contract Review Board (the Board sitting as the contract review board).

R.4.synopsis: Approves the construction project plan for a temporary deflection center in the Southeast Sandy building under the County's FAC-1 procedure, after an amendment passed unanimously. Commissioners Meieran and Brim-Edwards voted no.

R.5.synopsis: Resolution urging the Chair to use her authority to temporarily change the ambulance staffing protocol. It failed 1–3, with only Commissioner Brim-Edwards voting yes; the minutes' roll call doesn't list Commissioner Stegmann, who is recorded as absent.

R.2.synopsis: Approves the amended Homelessness Response System intergovernmental agreement with the City of Portland and the Homelessness Response Action Plan. Commissioner Meieran voted no.

Revisions to the Public Contract Review Board rules, with the Board sitting as the contract review board. The resolution failed: the minutes list Meieran voting no and Stegmann and Vega Pederson aye; Commissioner Beason isn't listed and is recorded as absent, and Commissioner Brim-Edwards was excused.

R.6.synopsis: Approves $400,000 from contingency for a three-year pilot enhanced services district in the Gateway neighborhood. The minutes name only Commissioner Brim-Edwards's no vote; the other commissioners present are recorded as Yea.

R.2.synopsis: Approves the Homelessness Response System intergovernmental agreement with the City of Portland and the Homelessness Response Action Plan, 4–1 with Commissioner Meieran voting no. Several amendments were voted on first, but the captioned minutes don't record those roll calls clearly enough to log. (The minutes list Chair Vega Pederson as excused at the start; the transcript shows her chairing and voting on this item.)

R.1.synopsis: Adopts Multnomah County's fiscal year 2025 budget and makes its appropriations, after a public hearing and roll calls on Board amendments, many of which failed 2–3 with Commissioners Meieran and Brim-Edwards voting yes. Commissioner Meieran voted no on adoption.

R.2.synopsis: Levies Multnomah County's property taxes for fiscal year 2025.

R.6.synopsis: Authorizes fiscal year 2024–2025 salary adjustments for County employees not covered by collective bargaining agreements.

R.7.synopsis: Approves the County's fee schedule for fiscal year 2025.

R.8.synopsis: Adopts the Multnomah County Library District's fiscal year 2025 budget and makes its appropriations, with the commissioners sitting as the district's governing body.

R.9.synopsis: Levies the Multnomah County Library District's property taxes for fiscal year 2025.

R.2.synopsis: Budget modification transferring cash for the 'Future of Work' program. The minutes name only Commissioner Brim-Edwards's no vote; the other commissioners present are recorded as Yea.
Approves the Library Capital Bond Program's East County Library construction plan under the County's FAC-1 procedure and authorizes the Chair to sign a guaranteed maximum price amendment.

R.7.synopsis: Consents to Chair Vega Pederson's appointment of Denise Pena as director of the Department of Community Justice.

R.1.synopsis: Approves Chair Vega Pederson's proposed fiscal year 2025 budget for submittal to the Tax Supervising and Conservation Commission, with the Board sitting as the Budget Committee. Commissioners Meieran and Brim-Edwards voted no.

R.2.synopsis: Approves the Multnomah County Library District's proposed fiscal year 2025 budget for submittal to the Tax Supervising and Conservation Commission. Commissioners Meieran and Brim-Edwards voted no.

R.3.synopsis: Second reading and adoption of an ordinance removing Section 11.514(B) from County Code Chapter 11 (Revenue and Taxation).

R.4.synopsis: Approves the construction project plan for the Montavilla Community Village alternative shelter site under the County's FAC-1 procedure. Commissioner Meieran voted no.

R.5.synopsis: Supplemental budget for the Montavilla Community Village alternative shelter, approved 3–1. Commissioner Meieran asked to put one more question after the vote was called and, when the Chair declined, voted no; Commissioner Brim-Edwards voted yes while objecting to that ruling. Commissioner Beason was excused.

R.6.synopsis: Increases a lease appropriation. Commissioner Meieran voted no.

Expresses the Board's concern about the impacts of the war in Gaza and calls for a ceasefire.

R.1.synopsis: Adds City of Portland Title 33 and comprehensive plan changes from the City's housing regulatory relief work to the County's zoning code and comprehensive plan.

R.2.synopsis: Approves the County's agreement with the City of Portland to amend the property tax exemption and system development charge codes for affordable housing, temporarily enabling homeownership opportunities for more households.

R.3.synopsis: Approves, as amended, the County's agreement with the City of Portland to amend the multiple-unit housing property tax exemption and inclusionary housing codes, with technical corrections and changes to the exemption. Passed 3–2 with Commissioners Meieran and Brim-Edwards voting no; the item was set aside and voted on later in the meeting.

Second reading and adoption of an ordinance amending the Preschool for All income tax (Code Chapter 11.500) to make administrative code changes.

Second reading and adoption of an ordinance adding the City of Portland's Floodplain Resilience Plan zoning changes to the County's zoning map and code.
